cards.explanation: The answer is the LORD's salvation. Verse 123 says he's “…looking for Your salvation, and for Your righteous promise.” So he's looking to the LORD for rescue, and the LORD's promise comes right along with it. That's a man who knows exactly where to point his eyes, friends.

The answer is the LORD's loving devotion. He says, “Deal with Your servant according to Your loving devotion, and teach me Your statutes.” Notice he doesn't bring a résumé, friends. He asks to be dealt with by who the LORD is, and he asks to be taught in the same breath.

The answer is True. Verse 125 says, “I am Your servant; give me understanding, that I may know Your testimonies.” He starts with who he is, the LORD's servant. Then he asks for understanding so he can know the testimonies. That's a servant asking for exactly what he needs.

The answer is False. The text gives a different reason: “It is time for the LORD to act, for they have broken Your law.” Nothing in verse 126 says his home was taken, friends. It's about the law being broken.

The answer is the purest gold. Verse 127 says, “Therefore I love Your commandments more than gold, even the purest gold.” He doesn't just say gold. He goes for the purest gold and still says he loves the commandments more. I stamp cookies for a living and even I know that's a big statement.
The answer is False. Verse 128 says, “Therefore I admire all Your precepts and hate every false way.” The word is all, friends. He admires every one of them.

The answer is hates. Verse 128 says he admires all the precepts “…and hate every false way.” Notice he's not lukewarm about it, bakers. He admires some things and he hates others, and he says so plainly.

The answer is the simple. Verse 130 says, “The unfolding of Your words gives light; it informs the simple.” You don't have to be fancy for it to work, friends. I think that's good news for anybody who's ever felt a little worn down, and I've been a worn-down stamper myself.

The answer is the LORD's commandments. Verse 131 says, “I open my mouth and pant, longing for Your commandments.” Panting like that is a big, loud kind of wanting, bakers. And what he wants is the LORD's commandments.

The answer is False. Verse 132 says, “Turn to me and show me mercy, as You do to those who love Your name.” He's asking the LORD to turn toward him and show him mercy. There's no asking for space in there at all, friends.

The answer is sin. Verse 133 says, “Order my steps in Your word; let no sin rule over me.” He asks for both in one breath, friends. He wants his steps ordered by the word, and he doesn't want sin ruling over him.

The answer is keep. Verse 134 says, “Redeem me from the oppression of man, that I may keep Your precepts.” Look at the order, bakers. First he asks to be redeemed, and then he says why: so he can keep the precepts. I think a man asking for rescue and a chance to keep the LORD's word in the same breath knows what he cares about.

The answer is True. Verse 136 says, “My eyes shed streams of tears because Your law is not obeyed.” Streams, not a sniffle, friends. I think this one hurts, and I'd say it's okay to just sit with it for a second.
The answer is False. Verse 138 says, “The testimonies You have laid down are righteous and altogether faithful.” Altogether faithful, friends, so there's no leftover part that isn't.

The answer is that his foes forget the LORD's words. Verse 139 says, “My zeal has consumed me because my foes forget Your words.” The zeal is about the LORD's words being forgotten, bakers. That's what the verse points to.
The answer is loves. Verse 140 says, “Your promise is completely pure; therefore Your servant loves it.” Pure promise, so he loves it. The verse puts those two together with a therefore, friends.
The answer is forget. Verse 141 says, “I am lowly and despised, but I do not forget Your precepts.” Lowly and despised, and he still holds on to the precepts, bakers. That's the word: forget.

The answer is True. Verse 142 says, “Your righteousness is everlasting and Your law is true.” Everlasting means it never ends, friends. I'd say that's worth a happy dance, and I'm doing one on my gold base right now.
The answer is his delight. Verse 143 says, “Trouble and distress have found me, but Your commandments are my delight.” The trouble is real, and so is the delight, friends. He says both in one breath.

The answer is so that he may live. Verse 144 says, “Your testimonies are righteous forever. Give me understanding, that I may live.” He asked for understanding back in verse 125 too, so this is the second time he asks, bakers. I think that tells you how much he wants it.
